LACEDÆMONE fuit Cynortas filius Argali, & Strabo l. ii. Pausan. l. 3. post eum Oebalus, à quo ad Menelaum fuere Tyn-darevs, Hypocoon, Castor & Pollux.

Quantum ad THESSALIAM, pulsus est ex Pausan. l. 7. ea Xuthus, Deucalionis ex Hellene F. nepos, & fugit Athenas, ibidemque ex Creusa ejus Regis F. Achæum & Ionem genuit. Fugit inde in Asiam & Phryxus, Deucalionis abnepos, novercæ ad Melicertam F. (in cujus honorem ludos Glaucus Bel-lerophontis pater instituit) omnia rapientis infi- dias cum Hella sorore (quæ submersa Hellefpon- to nomen imposuit) declinans. Sequentia sub Abimelecho vide.

ATHENIS Erechteus bellum Eleusiniis, a- pud quos nuper Celeus, & post eum Triptolemus regnaverat, intulit; & Eumolpum Thracem ma- gno barbarorum numero, ipsis suppetias feren- tem, immolatâ ex responso oraculi, ex Praxithea Lephisi Regis Thebani filia, Proserpinâ filiâ, vi- Pausan. in cit. Successit eiâ terra absorpto, seu fulminea a Atticis Sto- Jove Neptuni rogatu iꝯo, Cecrops II. qui Athe- baus jer- nienses in vicis habitantes, in duodecim urbes mon. 38. tribuit, coloniam in Eubæam deduxit, ibidem- que Athenas Diadas condidit. Praxitheæ illius præclara extant hodieque apud Lycurgum verba:

page.notes: Left-edge fragments (2591, 2590 and the partial column of notes on the left) belong to the other printed page and are not transcribed. Remaining text continues beyond this part. Marginal notes at the left edge are cut off in this part; only the fragments of the outer notes are visible and are not transcribed. The Greek lines are transcribed as far as legible; the first line's opening and the second line's accents are doubtful.
